text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, saying:
'Who is this who clouds my counsel with words that show no knowledge?
Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you will answer me.
Where were you when I laid the earth's foundations? Tell me, if you know so much.
Who set its measurements — surely you know! — or who stretched a measuring line across it?
What were its footings sunk into, or who set its cornerstone in place,
while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
Who shut the sea behind doors when it burst out from the womb,
when I dressed it in clouds and wrapped it in thick darkness,
when I set its boundaries and fitted it with bars and doors,
and said, "You may come this far and no farther; here your proud waves stop"?
Have you ever in your life commanded the morning, or shown the dawn its place,
so that it might grasp the edges of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
The earth is transformed like clay under a seal, and its features stand out like a folded garment.
Light is withheld from the wicked, and their raised arm is broken.
Have you gone down to the springs that feed the sea, or walked through the depths of the ocean floor?
Have the gates of death been shown to you? Have you seen the gates of deepest darkness?
Have you comprehended how vast the earth is? Tell me, if you know it all.
Which way leads to where light lives, and where is darkness's home,
so that you could take each to its own territory and know the paths to its house?
Surely you know, since you were already born then, and you have lived so very many years!
Have you entered the storerooms of the snow, or seen where the hail is kept in reserve,
which I hold back for times of trouble, for days of war and battle?
By what road is the light scattered, or the east wind spread out over the earth?
Who cuts a channel for the flood of rain, or a path for the thunderclap,
to bring rain on land where no one lives, on a desert with no one in it,
to satisfy the wasteland and desolate ground, and make the grass sprout there?
Does the rain have a father? Who fathers the drops of dew?
From whose womb does the ice come? Who gives birth to the frost of the sky,
when the waters turn hard as stone and the surface of the deep freezes over?
Can you tie the cords of the Pleiades together, or loosen the belt of Orion?
Can you bring out the constellations each in their season, or guide the Bear and its cubs across the sky?
Do you know the laws that govern the heavens? Can you put those laws into effect on earth?
Can you raise your voice to the clouds and call down a flood of water to cover you?
Can you send lightning bolts on their way, so that they report back to you, "Here we are"?
Who gave wisdom to the mind, or understanding to the heart?
Who is wise enough to count the clouds, or tip over the water jars of heaven,
when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods of earth stick together?
Can you hunt down prey for the lioness, or satisfy the hunger of her cubs,
as they crouch in their dens or lie in wait in the thicket?
Who provides the raven's food, when its young cry out to God and wander about with nothing to eat?'
